topic: Geometric Optics and Real-Time Refraction Tracing

object_x.derived_constraint: object must stay left of lens
object_x.label: Object horizontal position

f.label: Focal length (distance between lens center and focal points F, F')

image_type.derived: if v > 0: Real Inverted; if v < 0: Virtual Upright; if v = ∞: Undefined

srtc.R: A canvas with a central convex lens (thickness scales with focal length), an orange object arrow on the left, two green focal points F and F' draggable on the optical axis. Three principal rays are drawn from the object tip through the lens. A colored image arrow appears on the right (green for real, blue for virtual). An instrument dashboard shows live values of f, u, v, and M. A status tag shows the image type and orientation.
srtc.T: Dragging the orange object arrow moves it horizontally and vertically, changing u and object height. Dragging a focal point (F or F') changes f, reshaping both the lens bowing and all derived optical values simultaneously.
srtc.C: The thin lens equation 1/u + 1/v = 1/f is always satisfied. When u < f, the image distance v becomes negative (virtual image). When u = f, the image forms at infinity.
